source: ~/Desktop/FlintVellum/flintvellum-phase-2.md, Indeed postings for Role A and Role B; supported by PHASE-1.md; backend salary, crypto/AI priorities and test-first process updated by the owner in this conversation.
status: These are draft role outlines from a fictional company and hiring brief, not verified live vacancies. The pay figures below describe the proposed packages.

backend.intro: Build the services that connect a collector’s final bid to a completed crypto settlement. You will own auction and payment logic, solve the cases that operations cannot afford to get wrong, and use AI tools as part of your daily engineering work.
responsibilities: Own bid validation, reserve handling, auction closing and settlement services from design through production.
Build clear records for cryptocurrency payment events, confirmations, failed transfers and payout reconciliation.
Handle simultaneous bids, safe retries and duplicate events without losing or repeating a transaction.
Use AI coding assistants, research tools and review tools to investigate problems, build features and develop tests; check their output before it reaches production.
Work directly with operations to turn difficult settlement cases into reliable, maintainable services.
requirements: A working understanding of cryptocurrency is essential. Practical experience buying, holding or transferring crypto is strongly preferred; personal experience counts.

Understand wallets, addresses, networks, transaction fees, confirmations and the difference between Bitcoin, Ethereum and stablecoins. We value practical crypto knowledge more than an impressive list of frameworks.
Be AI-native in your working habits: use different AI tools for coding, research, debugging and review, and be able to explain where you verify or reject their output.
Be able to build, debug and maintain production backend services in Node.js and TypeScript, with sound SQL, transaction handling and accurate money calculations.
Explain your decisions clearly and take responsibility for the behaviour of the services you ship.
backend.context: The core stack is Node.js, TypeScript, Fastify and PostgreSQL, with Redis and BullMQ for background work and WebSockets for bid updates. The brief also includes AWS, Vitest and GitHub Actions. Practical crypto fluency and effective use of AI tools take priority over matching every item in the stack. This remains a senior individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Engineering.
backend.arrangements: £90,000–£170,000 annual base plus share options, with the offer reflecting relevant experience and scope. Full-time and remote. UK or EU candidates are preferred, international candidates are welcome, and overlap with UK working hours is required. Country-specific employment arrangements and any salary conversion would be confirmed before an offer. Share-option terms are separate from salary.
hiringProcess: Stage one is a technical test, completed before any conversation with Steve Mercer. It covers backend reasoning, practical cryptocurrency knowledge and how you use AI tools while checking the result.
Within one to two working days of submission, candidates will be notified whether they are moving to stage two: a conversation with Steve Mercer.
The test uses a fictional scenario. Candidates do not need to buy cryptocurrency, connect a wallet, reveal private keys or seed phrases, or transfer funds.

sales.intro: Build relationships with collectors and dealers who may consign watches, trading cards, or sports and film memorabilia. This is a phone-led role, following the seller relationship from the first conversation through to intake, a completed sale and repeat business.
responsibilities: Find and call collectors and dealers, and follow up on referrals and inbound enquiries.
Ask useful questions about the item, ownership, condition and the seller’s expectations.
Explain estimates, reserves, fees and payment timing without promising an auction result.
Secure consignment agreements and coordinate handover to specialists and operations.
Keep clear call notes, follow through on commitments and build a pipeline of repeat consignors.
requirements: A track record of closing by phone, typically five years or more, ideally in auctions, watch dealing, collectibles or another market involving valuable personal assets.
Evidence of building a pipeline, handling price objections and winning repeat business.
Confidence discussing valuable objects with collectors and dealers, with the judgement to involve a specialist when needed.
Consistent follow-up, accurate records and comfort with regular outbound calls.
sales.context: The salesperson owns the relationship; specialists approve authenticity and estimates. The proposed role reports to the Head of Sales and has no direct reports. Success means signed consignments that become completed sales, alongside relationships that bring sellers back.
sales.arrangements: Full-time and remote, with seller calls during UK business hours and occasional evening calls by agreement. International candidates are welcome, with UK or EU candidates preferred. Employment arrangements would need to be confirmed for the candidate’s country. On-target earnings include variable commission and are not a guaranteed salary; commission attribution, targets and payment terms would need to be set out in writing.
